chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Musa ibn Bakr from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you pray over the woman, stand at her head, and when you pray over the man, stand at his chest."

key_terms.صَلَّيْتَ: You prayed (specifically the funeral prayer in this context)

ai.seo_question: Where should the Imam stand during the funeral prayer for a woman versus a man?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the specific juristic etiquette (adab) for the funeral prayer, distinguishing the Imam's standing position based on gender to align with modesty and anatomical orientation. While the majority of Shia jurists consider this standing at the head for women and the chest for men to be recommended (mustahabb) rather than obligatory, it reflects the nuanced application of ritual purity and dignity in Shia fiqh. This distinction underscores the attention to detail in Shia ritual practice, ensuring the prayer is performed with both spiritual reverence and physical appropriateness.
